properties.IncidentOverview: A storm moved through northern Harney County on July 22; 2026; yielding hundreds of positive lightning strikes. The Bald Mountain Fire was discovered on the afternoon of July 23; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone; Rangeland Fire Protection Association and the Egypt Fire responded promptly but were unable to contain the fast moving wildfire. Southern Area Team 2 is responsible for management of the fire; along with the Stubble; Crater; Second Flats and Jackass Butte fires. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

A lightning storm moved through Eastern Oregon on July 15; 2026; igniting multiple fires. The Egypt Fire was discovered on the morning of July 16; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone responded promptly but were spread thin due to several other starts in the area. Southern Area Team 2 took command of the Egypt Fire on July 19 at 6 AM. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

U.S. Wildland Fire Service wildland firefighters are responding to the Island Fire; which was reported on July 25 at approximately 9 p.m. The fire is located about 25 miles southwest of Ehrenberg; Arizona; in the Cibola National Wildlife Refuge. The cause of the fire is under investigation. The fire is estimated to be approximately 2;815 acres and is 0% contained. The bridge on Hart Mine Road crossing the Colorado River burned and collapsed into the river. The area is closed to the public to allow firefighters to safely carry out suppression efforts. Wildland firefighters are actively working to suppress the fire and protect life; property; and natural and cultural resources. Engines; crews; and aircraft are responding to the wildfire. Additional wildland firefighting resources have been ordered to support suppression efforts. Active wildfire areas are always a No Drone Zone. When unauthorized drones are detected in the area; aerial firefighting operations are immediately grounded for safety; delaying response efforts and limiting our ability to protect lives; property; and natural resources.

The Castle Fire was first reported on July 22; 2026. It is currently estimated to be 1;550 acres. Hand-crews; engines; water tenders; dozers and a variety of other heavy equipment are on scene; with more requested. Crews continue to work on indirect containment lines. Dozer line was established on the southwestern flank of the fire. Central and Eastern Oregon; as well as other areas of the country have a high number of fires; so resources are limited; and may be responding from a long distance away. California Complex Incident Management has assumed management of the Fire as of 6:00 this morning. This team will be integrated with an International CIMT. Moderate temperatures have aided in overnight recovery and moderated fire growth in the morning hours. Firefighters are using tactics and strategies that provide the highest likelihood of success while mitigating risks to responders in this steep terrain. Crews and heavy equipment continue to strengthen direct and indirect lines where they can be defended and successfully contain the fire. Closure order #06-15-02-26-01 was issued for Area Closures: A portion of the Umpqua National Forest is closed near the Castle Fire (Little Black Rock and Castle Creek areas); as well as South Umpqua Falls Campground and Day Use Area. The purpose of this Order is to protect public and firefighter health and safety during active wildfire suppression operations. Visit the Umpqua Alerts and Notices page at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/alerts/castle-fire-closure - You may also click on the Closure Order (pdf) and Closure Order Map (pdf). Public Use Restrictions: As of Friday; July 24; 2026 the Umpqua National Forest moved to Public Use Restrictions (PURs) Stage 2 across the whole Forest. More Information is available at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/alerts/public-use-restrictions-stage-2 Smoke Impacts: With a significant number of fires burning within Oregon; please take steps to protect yourself from smoke. Smoke can irritate the eyes and lungs and worsen some medical conditions. People most at risk include infants and young children; people with heart or lung disease; older adults and pregnant people. Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on weather. Check current conditions on the U.S. Interagency Wildland Fire Air Quality Response Program ; the Oregon Smoke Information Blog ; DEQ’s Air Quality Index ; or by downloading the free OregonAIR app on your smartphone. About the Forest: The Umpqua National Forest protects 982;510 acres of forest across Douglas; Lane; and Jackson Counties. High Cascades glaciation; whitewater rapids; and explosive volcanic events have shaped the Forest's spectacular scenery and abundant natural resources. Verdant stands of hemlock; fir and cedar transition to forests of mixed conifers and hardwoods at lower elevations; while alpine ecosystems dominate high peaks like Mount Thielsen. The Forest's waterways and diverse ecosystems create desirable habitat for many species of fish and wildlife; in addition to providing outstanding recreational opportunities to our local communities and visitors.
